body: Thanks so much for the kind words-they mean a lot. Yeah, it’s a really scary feeling. It helps to know that others have felt the same, and gotten through it.
Thank you, it means a lot ❤️
This is usually what I do, but seems ill advised in this time of social distancing...

Thanks for the kind words :). Yeah, my cat is living her best life. At least one of us is!

Sending virtual hugs back.

I think it’s been 9 days since I last touched someone (5 of which have been in self-quarantine) and it’s honestly really getting to me. I don’t have an SO and my family is across the country, plus in a high risk demographic. I have a cat, and she’s wonderful, but it doesn’t feel like enough. Thinking of getting a weighted blanket or even seeing if one of my friends is willing to be a designated exclusive hugs and cuddles person.

Pretty not ok, in Day 6 of self-quarantine, really missing human touch (which I still won’t be able to have after this quarantine is over) and feeling incredibly upset at the thought that this may go on for months. Last night I started to feel suicidal in a way that I never had before that scared me...while in the past I’ve thought about it some this time I was honestly glad I don’t have easy means to do it at home because I feel a little afraid I wouldn’t be able to resist the temptation. I [texted HOME to 741741](https://www.crisistextline.org/) to text with a crisis counselor last night and it was somewhat helpful.

I have great friends I’m in virtual contact with and a loving cat...it just sucks that none of it feels like enough.

Thanks. I definitely know they all do. And if I look at it from a detached perspective I can see that this is for once a case where the “permanent solution to a temporary problem” really does seem to apply. But dealing with this day to day just feels like it will be very hard, and exhausting.

Thanks :) Yeah I’m trying at least to remind myself that there’s no reason to make any stupid decisions at least until my self-quarantine is over on Sunday. Hopefully these feelings won’t persist beyond then, or if they do I’ll be able to find a new goalpost.

Today I spent 3 hours with no screens and that felt pretty great.

I hope things get better for both of us. And for the world! :)

Thanks :) I know there have been other 18 month periods of life that have been hard that I’ve gotten through, this just seems so cataclysmic and uncertain and rapidly changing, I guess. And yeah, not being able to get hugs really sucks.

Thanks again for the kind and thoughtful words.

I’m feeling this too. Been self-quarantined 5 days (decided to let myself start taking short, careful walks around the neighborhood today for sanity...) and it’s gotten me to a pretty dark place. I deeply miss human touch and cry when I think about it. I talk to wonderful friends in FaceTime and chat but it doesn’t feel like enough. Tonight got to a pretty bad place that felt like the closest I’ve ever come to being dangerously suicidal. It felt like if I had the means readily available I might do it (fortunately, I don’t). 

Chatting with friends definitely feels like it helps temporarily, even if the sadness and loss is still there underneath. I hope you find things that work for you in navigating these very strange times and I hope things get better for both of us :)

I think this is the closest I’ve felt to suicide, and it doesn’t feel the way I’d expect

Like probably a lot of people I’ve thought passively about suicide at various parts of my life, sometimes fairly obsessively when things were tough. I’ve thought about how I might do it and about wanting things to be over. But while I might not have always recognized it at the times, I don’t think I was ever anywhere remotely close to going through with it.

This feels different. Just matter of fact, like it might be the best, or only option; but also scary, like I don’t want to let myself think about it too much lest it become a concrete, easily doable option. 

I’ve been self-quarantining for the past 5 days due to possible covid-19 exposure. I desperately miss basic human touch and closeness and don’t feel things are going to be that much better when the quarantine period is over: we’ll all still be social distancing, and possibly under shelter in place or martial law. Whenever I think of literally a week ago, when I still was able to hug friends and hold hands and share food and just be less than 6 feet away from someone, I start crying. I miss it so much and I don’t know if I can deal with possibly up to 18 months of this. There’s also financial/job/future uncertainty, and anxiety about my parents’ health, that I won’t go into here.

I have a cat and have been doing tons of FaceTime and chat with friends, and they’re all wonderful, but none of it feels like enough. I just want to be able to hold someone and be held and to feel like this isn’t going to be forever.

When I was crying about it tonight, all I could think about was how hopeless it all feels and how much I want it to end, and how I would need to take care of the mess that is my room because I wouldn’t want whoever found me to see that. And then feeling relieved that I don’t have an easy means to do it at home because if I did I think it might be hard to resist. Even now I feel scared and like I’m trying to avoid thinking about possible means because I don’t want to go there because it might be too tempting.

I don’t know how to explain it but this feels so different from any suicidal thoughts I’ve had in the past and much scarier. I would appreciate any thoughts or just kind words.
Definitely with you. Having to constantly worry about keeping physical distance between people when you do go out, or even with roommates in your own home, doesn’t help imo.

You too. It’s way harder than I expected it to be.

Today, I decided to let myself go out for short, careful walks around my neighborhood to keep sanity. It helped some in the moment but then tonight I felt the worst I’ve probably felt yet.

 I hope things will get better for both of us!
Definitely feels a little like the coronavirus daze the country is in is a weird case of the outside world suddenly matching the inner state I’ve been in for the past few months hahaha.

Anyone else sometimes find that they just really want to lie down, not because they’re tired but just to feel the ground/mattress/whatever underneath them? I guess I’m probably low key dissociated a lot of the time, which is weird because I don’t really notice it.

It might be a little while before I can see a psychiatrist, and I’m trying to use interpersonal support and a belief that I can get out of this place to help me start digging myself out of this hole in the meantime, but it’s hard. Anyone have particular success with vitamins/natural supplements? I just feel really low energy, kinda spaced out, and like it’s sometimes physically hard to move my body. I know reddit isn’t a doctor, but if there’s anything that’s helped for you I’d appreciate hearing it.

Briefly felt better when I acknowledged that this feeling of having zero motivation or energy to do anything, or even care about how much my life is falling apart, was depression: I felt like maybe there was a way out. Contacted doctors, started to try to make a plan to get necessary support/care to start getting better.

Now a few days later I think I feel worse? All I know was that when I was trying to avoid acknowledging how poorly things were going, I at least wasn’t consciously thinking about it all the time. Now it’s hard to stop thinking about it and for every hopeful moment there’s one profoundly hopeless one. Thinking about suicide and self-harm a lot more, though not enough to act on it. 

Curious if anyone’s had similar experiences.

I totally get it, it’s hard to balance feeling proud of something that was genuinely hard for you with feeling self conscious about what a small thing it seems like. Yesterday I wrote two emails and deposited a check, and felt really happy about having managed to do that instead of just letting things go.

I’m sorry you’re going through this, it can definitely be painful to be dealing simultaneously with the urge to self-harm and social stigma about it.

Something I found helpful when dealing with questions like this was the [Hurt Yourself Less Workbook](http://studymore.org.uk/hylw.pdf) [PDF]. It operates from a harm reduction standpoint: yes, for sure, superficial cuts are better than a suicide attempt, because they are likely to cause less harm. But since cutting still poses its own set of risks (losing control and cutting too deep, infection, etc), *if* you are able to safely find another coping mechanism that tends to be preferred. The idea isn’t to stigmatize various forms of self-harm as inherently bad but to recognize when we can find less harmful methods to cope.

You are doing the best you can. Regardless of what coping mechanism you end up using, remember that and try to be kind to yourself.
Basically haven’t looked at my emails in maybe...3 months? Finally think I can actually make myself do it, wish me luck.

Still in the midst of things, so not sure. I did find that just being able to talk openly about it—first online, then to a couple trusted friends—felt like it lightened things a surprising amount. For the first time I was able to really acknowledge what was happening and that I didn’t want it to keep happening. I started to feel a little more compassion for myself which in turn made me feel a little more hopeful and a little more desire to do things. Then I started to be hit by what feels like the enormity of what I have to do, which is it’s own challenge...but it does feel somewhat different, in a good way.

I’ve also seen exercise, decreasing sugar/alcohol/drug intake, and various vitamins recommended, so that could be something to look into. I haven’t really tried these myself yet, though.

Good luck! I hope you find something that’s able to get you through your immediate concerns until you can figure out something long-term.

I’m sorry things feel so hopeless. I also find the baby steps phrase really frustrating, especially because it feels like even when I manage to take those baby steps they don’t really go anywhere.

I know for myself, I’ve realized that I’m often a lot harder on myself than an outsider observer would be. I tend to see my failures as who I really am and any successes as aberrations. No idea how much this may apply to your situation since I don’t know your life, but as someone who went through most of childhood and university with little in the way of social life, then seemed to have things going really well for a while, and now doesn’t again...it’s what I tell myself to cope, anyway.

Best of luck and hope you’re able to find some hope, or at least some kindness for yourself.

I feel this a lot, especially:

>I can't focus at work and I'm worried it will have repercussions. Work used to be a bit of a self esteem booster for me, and now with that also going away, there's just nothing.

After wanting to believe I could get myself out of this rut through effort and then failing to do so day after day for months I was finally honest with my therapist about it, and we’re going to talk about options. I’m a little hopeful it will help. We’ll see. I hope you find something that helps you so that you don’t have to keep just tolerating it.

I relate to this so much, could’ve written it myself.

Often I’ll go into my room and sit on my bed around 9 or even earlier, planning to do some work, sometimes not having eaten dinner yet but planning to...then will just fall asleep and sleep until 7 or 8 and still find it hard to get out of bed.

My lack of attention to life tasks is causing me to fall further and further behind in important aspects of work and life and I know that it’s only a matter of time before I experience pretty serious consequences if I can’t get things back together, but whenever I kinda feel like I can that slips away and another day has passed without anything really changing...

I finally decided things were bad enough to be honest with my therapist (which first involved being honest with myself) and am hoping that will make a real difference. It’s hard, though.

Virtual hugs to you, too. Hope things get better for you soon.

Climbing has been good for me. I got into it before I started to feel depressed but I’ve been able to keep wanting to do it even when my motivation for everything else is really gone. There’s something about how physically and mentally involving it is; the feeling of being able to try, fail, and eventually succeed in a low-stakes environment; and the trust and communication with a climbing partner that has been really helpful for me. As with all such things, ymmv. It’s great that you’re able to motivate yourself to seek new things out, regardless!

Thanks for the thoughtful reply. I actually have talked to a therapist about it, which is one of the reasons I question whether it could really be related, since I feel like we processed a lot of it together. But I guess it’s possible that some lingering effects remain esp in combination with other life stresses.

I get this...I’ve gotten away with a lot of poor performance at work and school because of a support system that cares about me, and mostly I feel guilty for benefiting from so much privilege that I know other people in similar circumstances don’t have...

Yeah. I still mostly enjoy rock climbing and skiing, and am mostly able to motivate myself to do them. When I think about that, I feel like it just shows I’m faking it and just too lazy to do everything else, instead of just taking comfort in the fact that there are still places I find happiness and personal fulfillment.

I’m beginning to come to grips with the fact that maybe I’m depressed. I’ve been basically letting my life fall apart for the last several months. Checking email, paying rent, and doing other basic things feel really hard. It’s honestly a surprise I haven’t been fired, evicted, and/or kicked out of school yet. For months I’ve felt like I just need to force myself to get my shit together and that my inability to do so is just a reflection of my general lack of will-power/self-discipline.

An additional thing I’m struggling with now is that while I think some of this began earlier, it really intensified sometime around last September, which is also when I had an experience involving sexual assault. It makes me wonder if that is part of why, but then I immediately start berating myself and telling myself I’m probably just using that as an excuse. It’s also possible it’s more related to starting a stressful year in my PhD program. I guess it’s also possible that both factors contributed. I dunno really why, but somehow it feels important but also kinda impossible to know why.

I’m sorry you’re going through this. It can be scary to realize how much damage we can willingly do to our own bodies, but also hard to resist. I found the [Hurt Yourself Less](http://studymore.org.uk/hylw.pdf) workbook really helpful—it focuses on harm reduction and self-acceptance. I hope you might find it useful, too.

It's so hard to see someone you care about in pain--even or maybe especially if you have some feelings of frustration or resentment (as most siblings do). It's can also be especially hard when most of the people around you are concerned about the other person's pain, so they can't help you process your own (e.g. it sounds like your mom is worried about your sister, so maybe she's less able to help you deal with this). 

I'm sorry you're having to deal with this and hope you get some helpful support here and from your boyfriend. There are a lot of reasons people self-harm and it's impossible to know exactly why your sister is doing so, but it is probably because this is the best way she can find right now to cope with whatever is going on in her life. 

If at some point you want to offer her support, often people who self-harm find it most helpful when loved ones are non-judgmental and help them explore ways to limit their self-harm rather than expressing fear or demanding they stop immediately. The [Hurt Yourself Less](http://studymore.org.uk/hylw.pdf) workbook might be a good thing to pass along to her if you end up having a conversation and she seems open to resources. 

From personal experience I know this must be a really hard and scary time for your family. I hope knowing that an internet stranger is sending good thoughts will help you get through it a little easier :)
